highest_reported.source: Engel et al., Diverse beam search to find densest-known planar unit distance graphs, arXiv:2406.15317v3, Table 2, n=100 row; 22 found isomorphism classes.
highest_reported.reproduction_status: Reported in the paper but not reproduced because the linked Moser-lattice graph archive was inaccessible and the paper does not print the full n=100 point list. Kept separate from the exact 261-edge human baseline and reference.

best_human.source: Classical triangular-lattice patch, reconstructed from the unit triangular lattice generated by 1 and omega_1 in Engel et al., arXiv:2406.15317v3, §2.1 and Definition 2.4. The 10-by-10 restriction is reconstructed here; it is not claimed as their n=100 record.
best_human.provenance: Traditional human mathematical construction. The points are (i+j/2, sqrt(3)j/2) for 0<=i,j<10. This construction is a weak same-parameter baseline, not the published 439 record.
best_human.evidence_state: All 100 coordinates are saved and the 4,950 pairwise distances are checked exactly in Q(sqrt(3)). The three positive unit directions contribute 90+90+81=261 pairs.

best_public.source: Engel, Hammond-Lee, Su, Varga, and Zsámboki, arXiv:2406.15317v3, Table 2.
best_public.provenance: Traditional diverse GPU beam search on the Moser lattice. The paper's §6.1 discusses AI only as a possible future use of the graph database; no generative-AI role is reported for this search.
best_public.evidence_state: Reported as the highest edge count found for n=100, with 22 isomorphism classes. The coordinate witness is not available in the sources that could be retrieved, so the value is not reproduced by this task.

best_reproduced.verification_method: Replay the 10-by-10 triangular-lattice coordinates in Q(sqrt(3)); prove all 100 points distinct and check every unordered pair by exact reduction in the chosen real algebraic field.

frozen_human_baseline.evidence_state: Exact same-parameter traditional construction; 439 is retained separately as a reported but unreproduced value.

optimality_status.status: open; 439 is a reported lower bound and not a proof of the maximum
optimality_status.evidence: The 2025 paper's Table 2 reports 439 and 22 found isomorphism classes. Alexeev, Mixon, and Parshall, arXiv:2412.11914v2, prove exact values only through n=21. An October 2026 survey cites 439 as the largest reported n=100 value and notes no n=100 table in the 2026 rational-plane exploration paper.
optimality_status.limitations: The 439 coordinate witness was not recovered, and the source's search is restricted to the Moser lattice. No matching global upper-bound proof for unrestricted real-plane configurations was found.

rational_plane_exploration.scope_note: Large rational-plane graphs; no reported n=100 value in the paper or dataset survey

independent_quantity.method: independent Q(sqrt(3)) norm expansion for saved witnesses
